title: Stream sensitivity anchors and span telemetry orchestrator
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: As streaming responses become richer (function/tool calls, structured JSON envelopes, and progressive partial outputs), we lack a compact, privacy-preserving way to: 1) tie per-chunk metrics to tracing spans for end-to-end provenance, 2) surface redaction statistics without retaining full streamed payloads, and 3) maintain compatibility with older client chunk envelopes. Current approaches either store full transcript checkpoints (cost + compliance risk) or emit coarse session-level metrics that make diagnosing token-level regressions difficult.

Goal: Build a lightweight orchestrator that attaches a deterministic sensitivity anchor and span linkage to each emitted chunk/envelope. The anchor is a content-derived audit hash and sensitivity score computed at emission time; it allows operators to correlate metrics, trace spans, and redaction events without storing raw content. The orchestration layer must work for: plain text streaming, function/tool-calling chunks (tool call start/finish), and structured outputs (JSON blocks), and expose compatibility fallbacks for legacy clients.

Design overview:
- Per-chunk anchor: compute HMAC-SHA256 over normalized chunk metadata (stream_id, chunk_index, chunk_type, truncated content fingerprint) using a per-cluster audit key. We only persist the 8-byte base64 anchor and sensitivity tags (low|medium|high) — not payload. Anchor format: <anchor_v1>:<base64(8bytes)>.<sensitivity>.
- Span orchestration: when a streaming session begins, create a parent trace. Each chunk emission emits a lightweight span with the anchor attached as an attribute. Spans also include metrics: chunk_latency_ms, token_count, redact_matches, structured_parse_errors. Traces are exported to our tracing backend with retention matching privacy rules; payload-free anchors enable rehydration of trace->chunk relationships for troubleshooting.
- Redaction telemetry: integrate with existing redact pipeline to emit redact_hits for each chunk (counts and categories) and a redact_policy_version. Redaction decisions are recorded as counts associated with the anchor; full redacted text is never stored.
- Compatibility layer: introduce a chunk envelope translator that maps legacy chunk envelopes (old framing, no anchor) to the new envelope by generating anchor from received chunk data at the gateway edge. Legacy clients keep working; new consoles and audits consume anchors.
- Sampling & retention controls: default to 1% full-sample (for QA) and 100% anchor+counts emission. Sampling rate and full-sample windows controlled by feature flag per-customer and per-project.

Trade-offs considered:
- Computation overhead vs. observability depth: chosen deterministic 8-byte anchor reduces storage and transmission cost while still enabling unique session mapping. Using HMAC with cluster key provides non-reversible audit IDs.
- Real-time redaction vs. latency: redaction runs in the emission pipeline; we accept up to +6ms median overhead for secure redaction and anchor computation. If latency-sensitive routes opt-out, we fall back to token-level sampling-only mode.
- Backward compatibility: envelope translation adds CPU at the gateway; we scope translation to public API endpoints and add opt-out for private deployments that prefer client-side anchoring.

Implementation plan (high-level tasks):
1) Spec HMAC anchor format and key rotation policy (security review mandatory).
2) Implement anchor generator module in runtime emission layer (C++/Rust path) and a JS shim in the gateway for legacy envelopes.
3) Instrument per-chunk span creation and metrics; add metrics to our exporter (chunk_latency_ms, token_rate, redact_hits, parse_errors).
4) Add redact telemetry hooks to the redaction service to produce counts tied to anchor.
5) Add console views: per-anchor drilldown, aggregated sensitivity heatmaps, and per-route sampling controls.
6) QA + canary: rollout to low-traffic region, verify metrics correlation and PII non-retention.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every emitted chunk in canary traffic contains an anchor attribute and emits a span with at least chunk_latency_ms and token_count.
- Anchor uniqueness collision rate < 1e-9 across 30 days in canary volume.
- Redaction telemetry for chunks is available in the trace and shows consistent counts; no raw content stored in logs or metrics.
- Latency regression: median token emit latency increase <= 8ms on default routes.
- Backcompat: legacy client requests receive translated envelopes and anchors for >= 95% of translated chunks.

Observability & alerts:
- New SLOs: anchor_ingest_success_rate (>99.9%), redact_telemetry_delivery (>99.5%), span_emit_failure_rate (<0.1%).
- Dashboards: per-route chunk latency histograms, redact_hit_rate by sensitivity, anchor-to-span reconciliation.

Security & compliance notes:
- HMAC keys stored in KMS with strict rotation and auditor role separation.
- Anchors are non-reversible; however legal requests requiring content will follow established process (key escrow under warrant only).
- Security review required before canary (flag set above).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement anchor generator and unit tests; security review kickoff.
- Week 2: implement span emit + redaction telemetry hooks; internal smoke tests.
- Week 3: gateway translator and console visualizations; small canary (5% traffic low-risk customers).
- Week 4: expand canary to 25% and run compliance audit; collect metrics, tweak sample rates.
- Week 5: GA for hosted API with customer opt-in and default anchor emission.
